title: Role — JVM / Spring Boot
description: Any Spring Boot (Micrometer) application whose Prometheus endpoint the host collector reads (portablevps.telemetry.prometheusTargets): JVM memory, GC, threads and CPU; the Hikari pool; HTTP server requests; Tomcat, executors and scheduled tasks; log events by level. Pick the service at the top; links can pass ?var-service=<name>.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the JVM started (the youngest instance when several hosts are selected). A reset is a restart.

panels.title: Heap used
panels.description: Heap in use as a share of the maximum heap. G1 runs high between collections; what matters is the level after GC (Memory row).

panels.title: Process CPU
panels.description: The JVM's CPU use as a share of all the machine's cores.

panels.title: GC pause share
panels.description: Share of wall time the application was paused for garbage collection. Above a few percent the heap is too small or something allocates hard.

panels.title: DB pool in use
panels.description: Hikari connections checked out as a share of the pools' maximum. Pinned at 100% means requests queue for a connection.

panels.title: Errors logged (range)
panels.description: ERROR lines the application logged over the selected range (Logback).

panels.title: Heap by pool
panels.description: Heap in use per pool (stacked) against the maximum heap.

panels.title: Non-heap by pool
panels.description: Metaspace, compressed class space and the code cache. Metaspace that only grows points at a class-loader leak.

panels.title: Heap after GC
panels.description: What survives a collection: the trend that matters for heap sizing. A floor that keeps rising is a leak.

panels.title: Allocation & promotion
panels.description: Rate of new allocation in the young generation and of objects promoted to the old generation.

panels.title: Direct & mapped buffers
panels.description: Off-heap NIO buffers (Netty, file channels). They count against the container's memory, not the heap.

panels.title: Container memory
panels.description: Memory of every container of this service (podman stats), for comparison with heap + non-heap + buffers. Empty when the application does not run in a container.

panels.title: GC pauses / s
panels.description: Stop-the-world pauses per second by collector and kind.

panels.title: GC pause time share
panels.description: Share of wall time spent paused, per collector.

panels.title: Longest pause
panels.description: The longest pause in Micrometer's recent window, by collector and cause; and the share of time concurrent GC threads ran (not a pause).

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Live, daemon and peak thread counts. Live threads that only climb are a thread leak.

panels.title: Thread states
panels.description: Threads per state. Many blocked threads means lock contention.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: The JVM's and the whole machine's CPU, each as a share of all cores.

panels.title: Open files & classes
panels.description: File descriptors the JVM holds open (its limit is process_files_max_files, usually far above) and classes currently loaded. Either climbing without end is a leak.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Connections checked out (active), ready (idle), threads waiting for one (pending), against the pool maximum.

panels.title: Acquire time
panels.description: How long getting a connection from the pool took: mean over the interval and the recent maximum. Anything above milliseconds means the pool is exhausted.

targets.expr: sum by (pool) (rate(hikaricp_connections_acquire_seconds_sum{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pool) (rate(hikaricp_connections_acquire_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Timeouts, usage & creation
panels.description: Requests that gave up waiting for a connection (should be zero); how long a connection is held per use; how long opening one took.

targets.expr: sum by (pool) (rate(hikaricp_connections_usage_seconds_sum{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pool) (rate(hikaricp_connections_usage_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (pool) (rate(hikaricp_connections_creation_seconds_sum{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pool) (rate(hikaricp_connections_creation_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Requests by status
panels.description: Requests the application served, per status code (Micrometer http.server.requests).

panels.title: Errors by outcome
panels.description: Requests that ended as a client or server error, and those that raised an exception, by exception class.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Server-side request duration: mean and recent maximum always; p95/p99 only when the application publishes histogram buckets for http.server.requests.

panels.title: Endpoints (selected range)
panels.description: Every endpoint (Spring's URI template) over the selected range: request rate, 5xx share, mean and worst duration.

targets.expr: (sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host", status=~"5.."}[$__range])) or sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range]))

sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range])) / sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Tomcat sessions
panels.description: HTTP sessions held by embedded Tomcat. Rejected sessions mean maxActiveSessions was reached.

panels.title: Executors
panels.description: Spring's task executors: threads busy, tasks waiting, and the pool's maximum (left out when unbounded).

panels.title: Scheduled tasks
panels.description: Mean duration of each @Scheduled method; failing runs appear as their own series (per second, by exception).

targets.expr: sum by (code_function) (rate(tasks_scheduled_execution_seconds_sum{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (code_function) (rate(tasks_scheduled_execution_seconds_count{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Log events by level
panels.description: Lines logged per minute by level, from Logback's own counter (only levels that are enabled are counted).

panels.title: Warnings & errors / min
panels.description: Only WARN and ERROR, so a burst is not hidden under INFO.
